adjudication_label: Deposition temperature and stress evolution in irradiation
canonical_question: Why was room temperature deposition chosen for the films, and could this introduce residual stresses that confound the irradiation results at 1073 K?

question_variants.question: Why was room temperature deposition chosen for the films, and could this introduce residual stresses that confound the irradiation results at 1073 K?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states deposition was at room temperature but does not explain the rationale or discuss the impact of residual stress on subsequent high-temperature irradiation results.

answers.answer: The paper notes deposition was performed at room temperature, but does not justify this choice or analyze its effect on residual stress relative to irradiation at 1073 K.
answers.boundary_limitation: No discussion of stress confounding factors.
evidence_spans: A detailed characterization of the morphology and phase details of the as-deposited HEA films results in a bimodal grain size distribution with ~70% of the grains with size in the nanocrystalline regime (≤100 nm) and some regions of ultrafine grain sizes (100 to 500 nm) with an underlying single-phase BCC, with a lattice constant of ~3.2 Å
APT confirmed the EDS results, showing a film composition of 38% (±0.09) W, 36% (±0.09) Ta, 15% (±0.05) Cr, and 11% (±0.05) V.
The morphology is composed of very distinct compositional striations (layering) within the grains of ~4-nm thickness, which was not observed in EDS.

source_evidence_spans: The deposition was performed at room temperature
